name: Courtesy Residency for Family of a Lebanese Woman Married to a Foreigner

requirements.blocker_text: Foreign husbands and children of a Lebanese woman may obtain a free 'courtesy residency' permit under Decree No. 4186 (2010), issued through General Security. This exists because a Lebanese woman cannot pass her nationality to her foreign husband or (legitimate) children -- unlike a Lebanese man, whose foreign wife acquires Lebanese nationality outright (see lb_citizenship_by_marriage.json). The permit must be periodically renewed (every 1-3 years depending on the holder's passport expiry) and does not grant citizenship or equal legal status; holders remain classified as foreign nationals for employment, healthcare, education, and property purposes.
requirements.fix_path: Apply to General Security for courtesy residency under Decree No. 4186/2010, supported by proof of marriage to, or filiation from, a Lebanese woman.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate or proof of filiation from a Lebanese mother

outcome.duration_length: 1-3 years depending on the holder's passport expiry date, renewable

sources.title: Human Rights Watch -- describes Decree No. 4186 (2010) establishing free 'courtesy residency' permits for husbands and children of Lebanese women, renewed every 1-3 years, not conferring citizenship or equal legal status; notes a 2011 Labor Ministry regulation giving discretion to grant work permits in reserved professions

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Lebanon). STATUS: DRAFT -- this route's only located source is an NGO report (tier 4), not the decree text itself or a General Security page describing it (General Security's own site lists 'Courtesy Residence' as a residency category by name but the specific page content on requirements was not available in this build) -- the decree number, year, and mechanism are specifically and consistently identified (not a vague secondhand claim), but a tier-1 government citation should be treated as a priority follow-up for this route. MARQUEE FINDING, THE CLEAREST ILLUSTRATION IN THIS DATASET OF THE GAP BETWEEN 'HAS A RESIDENCY OPTION' AND 'HAS EQUAL RIGHTS': this route exists ONLY because Lebanese nationality law denies Lebanese women the ability to pass citizenship to their foreign husbands or legitimate children -- the 'family reunification' available to her is a renewable, revocable RESIDENCY permit, not citizenship, in direct contrast to a Lebanese man's foreign wife, who becomes a citizen outright after 1 year with no discretion involved (lb_citizenship_by_marriage.json). work_rights set 'restricted' since foreign husbands historically had to pledge not to work, with a 2011 regulation only discretionarily permitting work in reserved professions, renewed annually with no guarantee; family_can_work set false reflecting that baseline restriction, though this may now be less absolute in practice than the pledge-era rule the source primarily describes.
